story_thesis: Bath & Body Works' new $500m repurchase authorisation must be tested against shrinking core-store sales, margin pressure, seasonal cash conversion, debt and inventory risk.

identity.accounting: US GAAP with company-defined adjusted measures

candidate_review.selection_reason: Fresh results create a distinct retail capital-allocation question: a new $500m buyback authorisation arrives before core-store sales, margin and year-to-date cash conversion have recovered.

duplicate_check: Checked the editorial topic index, content inventories, actual related content, past 14 days, live finance catalogue, publication records, open and merged PRs and concurrent Compound/FairPath records. No Bath & Body Works analysis, profile or active attempt answers this question; no /stocks/bbwi/ URL was invented.

claim_checks.claim: Q3 net sales $1.577bn, down 1.0%; US/Canada stores $1.169bn, down 4.3%; direct up 2.6%; international/other up 39.3%
GAAP operating income $108m vs $161m and gross margin about 40.5% vs 41.3%
Nine-month OCF $251m and capex $155m imply $96m simple free cash flow
FY outlook approximately $815m OCF less $215m capex equals $600m company-defined free cash flow
$500m authorisation equals about 83% of FY FCF outlook, 1.6x cash and more than 5x nine-month simple FCF
claim_checks.result: verified Compound comparisons; authorisation not treated as completed spend

claim_checks.claim: Nine-month debt repayment $542m, dividends $120m and buybacks $59m; quarter-end cash $318m
Inventory $1.281bn vs $1.251bn, up 2.4%, while quarterly sales declined

fact_check_notes: Buyback authorisation is permission, not an obligation or completed purchase.
Shareholders' deficit is not represented as insolvency.
Full-year cash generation is guidance and holiday-dependent, not cash already received.
